# CEVA Logistics opens Derby distribution centre for UK eCommerce 

 

> CEVA Logistics opens Derby distribution centre for UK eCommerce 

CEVA Logistics has opened a new 508,000-square-foot distribution centre in Derby, expanding its UK contract logistics network to support growing demand from the eCommerce sector.

The facility is scheduled to become fully operational in August 2026. It will provide storage, handling and distribution services for global eCommerce customers, helping speed up deliveries across the UK.

The new operation is expected to create around 300 jobs, strengthening the regional logistics sector while supporting CEVA’s continued investment in the UK market.

The warehouse was designed with sustainability and scalability in mind. It has achieved BREEAM Excellent and EPC A+ certifications and features a rooftop solar installation to reduce energy consumption.

# Family food business opens landmark DC

Posted on Monday 3 August 2026 Share: 

Family-owned fine foods manufacturer and distributor, Bramble Foods has opened a new 67,000 ft2 distribution centre in Market Harborough, Leicestershire, East Midlands.

By Liza Helps, Property Editor, Logistics Matters

THE COMPANY pre-let the facility on the final phase of Leicestershire Council’s Airfield Business Park last year. It currently leases a unit on and will be taking the additional new unit to further expand their growing business.

The state-of-the-art facility becomes Bramble Foods’ main national distribution hub, significantly increasing warehousing and distribution capacity while supporting the company’s expanding portfolio of premium food brands which includes Whitakers Chocolates, The Bay Tree and Lings.

Airfield Business Park was first opened in 2019 and is home to 14 businesses.

The new facility known as Lancaster House includes a number of sustainability features and boasts an EPC A+ rating of A+, a 50kW solar array that should save between 45,000 and 50,000 kWh a year as well as two electric vehicle charging points.

# Translink Express makes four senior appointments

Leicestershire logistics firm Translink Express Logistics has made four senior appointments following 32 per cent growth over the past two years.

Lee Barrett has been promoted to head of traffic; Dan Green takes the newly created role of head of project management; and Shanice Walsh becomes head of operations.

Ryan Wallis has also joined the family-owned business as head of warehousing.

The new management team will take responsibility for the day-to-day running of Translink Express, allowing its directors to focus more closely on long-term strategy as the business approaches its 40th anniversary.

Chris Hobbis, director at Translink Express Logistics, said: “In two years we’ve seen record growth – just shy of 32 per cent, which is phenomenal.

# DC Spotlight | Darlington, UK

- Darlington, UK
- · 3 min read

Designed with both sustainability and people in mind, the site reflects our ongoing commitment to responsible operations and a positive employee experience. 

Spanning nearly 140,000 square feet, the facility supports more than 200 restaurants and has been designed and constructed to BREEAM Excellent Net‑Zero Carbon Construction standards, supporting our journey toward net zero goals.

# Automation with a purpose: why sustainability must be at the heart of the modern warehouse

Posted on Tuesday 1 September 2026 Share: 

The warehouse has undergone a remarkable transformation over the last decade, says Yusen Logistics UK.

ONCE VIEWED primarily as a storage location within the supply chain, today’s warehouse has become a critical hub for operational excellence, customer experience, business resilience and sustainability. As supply chains become increasingly complex, organisations are under growing pressure to deliver greater speed, accuracy and flexibility while reducing environmental impact and controlling costs.

For many businesses, warehouse automation has become a key part of the solution. However, automation alone is no longer enough.

The real opportunity lies in combining automation, digitalisation and sustainability to create facilities that are not only operationally efficient but capable of supporting long-term business and environmental goals.
